notes: PSA 5.5 ng/mL. PI-RADS 5. PSAD 0.12. Prostate volume 49 mL. DRE nodus. csPCa 0.81.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer management options following recent biopsy and MRI findings.

The patient is a 64-year-old hospital porter with a history of hypercholesterolaemia managed with statin therapy. He reports a gradual increase in PSA levels over the past two years, rising from 1.6 ng/mL to the current 5.5 ng/mL. He lives in a ground-floor apartment with his partner and maintains an active lifestyle, walking 45 minutes daily. Socially, he consumes approximately 14 units of alcohol per week and is an ex-smoker, having quit in 2022 after a 37 pack-year history. He denies any lower urinary tract symptoms, with an IPSS score of 0. Recent outpatient visits included an orthopaedic follow-up for knee issues and a routine chest X-ray. He has a visual impairment requiring large-print correspondence.

On DRE, a discrete nodule is palpable in the left peripheral zone, consistent with clinical stage cT2a. The prostate volume is estimated at approximately 49 mL. General examination reveals a well-nourished male with stable vital signs and no signs of metastatic disease.
